inspect-one.caption: Look closely: both trays weigh the same.
inspect-one.speechText: Look closely at this balanced scale. Everything on the left tray weighs the same as everything on the right tray.

inspect-many.caption: Look closely: every scale is balanced.
inspect-many.speechText: Look closely at these balanced scales. On every scale, the left tray weighs the same as the right tray.

substitute.caption: Replace one equal load with the other.
substitute.speechText: The highlighted loads weigh the same. We can replace one with the other, and the scale will stay balanced.

add-scales.caption: Move the Use scale onto the Working scale.
add-scales.speechText: Move the loads from the scale marked Use onto the matching trays of the scale marked Working. Left joins left, and right joins right. The Working scale stays balanced.

subtract-scales.caption: Use one scale to remove matching loads from the Working scale.
subtract-scales.speechText: Use the gold scale as a guide. On the purple Working scale, remove the matching left-tray loads and the matching right-tray loads. The Working scale stays balanced.

cancel-matches.caption: Remove the highlighted load from each tray.
cancel-matches.speechText: The highlighted animals appear on both trays. Remove them from each tray. The remaining loads will still balance.

regroup-2.caption: Circle 2 copies of the group we need.
regroup-2.speechText: The left tray contains two copies of the group we need. Circle those groups. Then split the right tray into two equal groups.

regroup-3.caption: Circle 3 copies of the group we need.
regroup-3.speechText: The left tray contains three copies of the group we need. Circle those groups. Then split the right tray into three equal groups.

regroup-4.caption: Circle 4 copies of the group we need.
regroup-4.speechText: The left tray contains four copies of the group we need. Circle those groups. Then split the right tray into four equal groups.

split-2.caption: Keep 1 of the 2 equal groups on each tray.
split-2.speechText: Each tray now has two equal groups. Keep one group on each tray. Those two groups will still balance.

split-3.caption: Keep 1 of the 3 equal groups on each tray.
split-3.speechText: Each tray now has three equal groups. Keep one group on each tray. Those two groups will still balance.

split-4.caption: Keep 1 of the 4 equal groups on each tray.
split-4.speechText: Each tray now has four equal groups. Keep one group on each tray. Those two groups will still balance.

strategy-split-evenly.caption: Make 2 equal groups on each tray.
strategy-split-evenly.speechText: There are two rabbits on the left and four chicks on the right. Make two equal groups on each tray. Each group has one rabbit and two chicks, so one rabbit balances two chicks.

strategy-cancel-matches.caption: A fox is on both trays. Remove one from each.
strategy-cancel-matches.speechText: A fox appears on each tray. Remove one fox from the left and one fox from the right. The remaining cat balances three chicks.

strategy-substitution.caption: Replace each fox with 2 chicks.
strategy-substitution.speechText: One fox balances two chicks. On the second scale, replace each fox with two chicks. Two foxes become four chicks, so the rabbit balances four chicks.

strategy-create-combo.caption: Circle 3 cat-and-bear groups.
strategy-create-combo.speechText: The left tray has three cats and three bears. Circle three groups with one cat and one bear in each. Split the fifteen beetles into three equal groups. One cat-and-bear group balances five beetles.

strategy-add-scales.caption: Add the scales to put cats and bears together.
strategy-add-scales.speechText: We need a cat and a bear together, but neither scale has that group. Move scale two onto scale one, left tray to left tray and right tray to right tray. Because both scales balance, the combined scale balances too.

strategy-subtract-scales.caption: Remove scale 2's loads from scale 1.
strategy-subtract-scales.speechText: Scale one has three cats and four bears balancing seven beetles. Remove the loads from scale two: one cat and two bears from the left, and three beetles from the right. Two cats and two bears still balance four beetles.

conclude.caption: Balanced — we found the answer.
conclude.speechText: The scale is still balanced. We found the answer.
